drivers.name: Material Rewards
drivers.definition: Refers to the desire for financial security, wealth, and the ability to enjoy a high standard of living. People driven by material rewards make career choices that enhance their economic well-being. They seek roles with competitive compensation and are often willing to take on challenging or less fulfilling work if it provides significant financial returns.
drivers.blurb: Good pay and the lifestyle it buys keep you going.
drivers.strengthZones: Sales, high-commission roles, entrepreneurship, competitive industries
drivers.families: Sales & retail, commercial roles, high-income tracks

drivers.name: Power / Influence
drivers.definition: Reflects the motivation to shape decisions, direct people or resources, and play a central role in key choices. These individuals aim for positions where they can influence outcomes, set direction, and make important decisions. Confident and proactive, they thrive in leadership, strategic, or policy-making roles.
drivers.blurb: You want a say in where things go, and to lead people there.
drivers.strengthZones: Supervisory roles, team leads, managerial tracks, operations control

drivers.name: Meaning / Purpose
drivers.definition: Centers on being motivated by work that aligns with personal beliefs, values, or a sense of higher purpose. These individuals want to make a meaningful contribution through social impact, education, sustainability, or ethical work. Personal fulfillment matters more than short-term rewards.
drivers.blurb: Work has to matter. You want to make a real difference.
drivers.strengthZones: CSR, NGOs, climate action, education, public sector, mission-driven roles

drivers.name: Expertise
drivers.definition: Reflects the desire to build deep knowledge and skills in a specific field. People with this driver focus on developing and maintaining specialist capabilities, preferring to work within their areas of strength. Their greatest satisfaction comes from being recognized as credible experts and staying current through continuous learning.
drivers.blurb: You want to master your craft and be the go-to person for it.
drivers.strengthZones: Technical specialists, analysts, engineers, finance experts, niche consulting
drivers.families: Specialist tracks, technical roles, finance, engineering

drivers.name: Creativity
drivers.definition: Represents the motivation to generate new ideas, solutions, or original work. Creative individuals thrive on solving problems in new ways, pushing boundaries, and bringing unique ideas to life, whether through product design, entrepreneurship, research, or artistic pursuits.
drivers.blurb: You bring fresh ideas to life and leave your signature on the work.

drivers.name: Affiliation
drivers.definition: Highlights the value placed on close, supportive relationships at work. People with this driver prioritize trust, collaboration, and human connection. They often choose to stay in roles because of the people they work with and derive a sense of purpose through relationships rather than hierarchy.
drivers.blurb: The people you work with make or break a job for you.
drivers.strengthZones: Customer service, teaching, people management, HR, hospitality

drivers.name: Autonomy
drivers.definition: Reflects the desire to control one’s time, decisions, and work methods. People with this driver thrive in environments that allow them to make their own choices, often avoiding rigid hierarchies and bureaucracy. They excel in roles like freelancing, consulting, or entrepreneurship where independence is valued.
drivers.blurb: You want control over your time, decisions and how you work.

drivers.name: Security
drivers.definition: Focuses on valuing stability and a clear sense of the future. These individuals prioritize avoiding unnecessary risks and ensuring long-term reliability. They often seek employers known for stability and prefer well-defined career paths that offer predictability and peace of mind.
drivers.blurb: You like stability, clear paths and knowing where you stand.
drivers.strengthZones: Government jobs, large corporates, banking, administrative operations

drivers.name: Status
drivers.definition: Reflects the desire to be acknowledged, respected, and admired by others. People with this driver are motivated by visible recognition: titles, awards, networks, or association with prestigious institutions. They actively build their reputation and seek opportunities that elevate their professional profile.
drivers.strengthZones: Client-facing roles, leadership, public representation, luxury sectors

archetypes.name: The People-First Service Builder
archetypes.roles: Customer service, client success, HR service, training, hospitality, community operations
archetypes.redFlags: Solitary specialist roles with little people contact; high-risk startups
archetypes.summary: You do your best work with people you trust, somewhere steady. Best-fit roles: customer service, client success, HR service, training, hospitality and community operations.

archetypes.name: The Commercial Rainmaker
archetypes.roles: Retail & B2C/B2B sales, business development, key accounts, luxury, revenue leadership
archetypes.redFlags: Low-upside admin roles; back-office analyst work with no customer exposure
archetypes.summary: You chase big wins and like being seen for them. Best-fit roles: retail and B2B sales, business development, key accounts, luxury and revenue leadership.

archetypes.name: The Specialist Operator
archetypes.roles: Technical specialist, finance/ops analyst, engineering, compliance, process excellence
archetypes.redFlags: Highly ambiguous “build-as-you-go” creative roles; pure sales
archetypes.summary: You go deep, get it right and like a clear path. Best-fit roles: technical specialist, finance or ops analyst, engineering, compliance and process excellence.

archetypes.name: The Creative Pathfinder
archetypes.roles: Product/design, marketing/content, R&D/innovation, creative consultancy, founder
archetypes.redFlags: Rigid bureaucracy; narrow repetitive tasks with no room for ideas
archetypes.summary: You light up when you can create, try new things and own how you work. Best-fit roles: product and design, marketing and content, R&D, creative consultancy, founding something.

archetypes.name: The Purpose-Driven Community Leader
archetypes.roles: Education/edtech, NGOs, climate/sustainability, public service, L&D, social programs
archetypes.redFlags: Purely money/status-driven cultures; hard-sell commercial roles
archetypes.summary: You want your work to matter and to bring people with you. Best-fit roles: education and edtech, NGOs, climate and sustainability, public service, L&D and social programmes.

archetypes.name: The Strategic Leader
archetypes.roles: Senior leadership, strategy, policy, business unit heads, organizational shapers, entrepreneurial ventures
archetypes.redFlags: Roles with low autonomy, low visibility, or purely operational with no decision-making scope
archetypes.summary: You want to set direction and be the one people look to. Best-fit roles: senior leadership, strategy, policy, business unit heads and entrepreneurial ventures.
